name: Suwawa
confidence_why: Rangubang et al. 2001, the dedicated phonology of Suwawa, find stress unpredictable and list three-syllable words stressed on the last, the second-last and the third-last syllable, whereas the shorter and older grammar sketch of Kasim et al. 1981 gives a fixed high pitch on the penult of two-syllable words and the antepenult of longer ones, and Sneddon & Usup 1986 say nothing about Suwawa stress, so the fuller 2001 description is followed while a real disagreement about the type of system remains.

catalog_quote: Rangubang et al. 2001, sec. 3.4 (pp. 55-56): "Berdasarkan data yang dikumpulkan, tidak dijumpai adanya tekanan, nada, dan panjang pendeknya bunyi yang dapat mengubah arti suatu kata. Walaupun demikian, tidak dapat dikatakan bahwa tekanan dalam bahasa Suwawa tidak fonemis. Dengan demikian, tekanan pada bahasa Suwawa tidak tetap atau tidak dapat diprakirakan. Artinya, tekanan dalam bahasa Suwawa tidak seperti dalam bahasa Indonesia yang pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku kedua dari belakang. ... tempat tekanan tidak dapat diprakirakan. Tekanan dalam bahasa Suwawa dianggap fonemis. ... a. Kata bersuku tiga yang tekanannya jatuh pada suku terakhir (ultima). [moho'ha] 'heran' [ogi'na] 'ingin' ... b. ... (penultima). [ti'gogo] 'leher' ... [bu'ława] 'emas' [mo'puha] 'merah' ... c. ... (prapenultima). ['watopo] 'atap' ..." Kasim et al. 1981, sec. 3.5 (pp. 22-23): "Di sini yang akan dibicarakan hanyalah di mana jatuhnya tekanan pada kata, atau hanya titi nada saja. ... Nada itu ditentukan oleh jumlah suku kata. (1) Bila terdiri dari dua suku kata maka nada tinggi terdapat pada suku kedua dari belakang. w u l u [3 2] 'kepala' ... (2) Bila terdiri dari tiga suku kata maka nada tinggi pada suku ketiga dari belakang. d u t u n a [3 2 1] 'sungai' ... (3) Bila terdiri dari empat suku kata maka nada tinggi tetap pada suku ketiga dari belakang. p e y a b u q o [2 3 2 1] 'debu' ..." Kasim et al. 1981, sec. 3.4.1 (p. 22): "(3) Yang terdiri dari tiga suku kata: ... mo-pu-ha 'merah' ..."

new_statements.quote: Berdasarkan data yang dikumpulkan, tidak dijumpai adanya tekanan, nada, dan panjang pendeknya bunyi yang dapat mengubah arti suatu kata. Walaupun demikian, tidak dapat dikatakan bahwa tekanan dalam bahasa Suwawa tidak fonemis. Dengan demikian, tekanan pada bahasa Suwawa tidak tetap atau tidak dapat diprakirakan. Artinya, tekanan dalam bahasa Suwawa tidak seperti dalam bahasa Indonesia yang pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku kedua dari belakang. [...] contoh beberapa kata bahasa Suwawa yang bersuku tiga yang tekanannya jatuh pada suku terakhir (ultima), suku kedua dari akhir (penultima), dan suku ketiga dari akhir (prapenultima). [moho'ha] 'heran' ... [bu'lawa] 'emas' ... ['watopo] 'atap'
new_statements.translation: On the basis of the data collected, no stress, pitch or length was found that can change the meaning of a word. Nevertheless, it cannot be said that stress in Suwawa is not phonemic. Thus stress in Suwawa is not fixed, i.e. cannot be predicted. That is, stress in Suwawa is not like Indonesian, where stress generally falls on the second syllable from the end. [...] examples of trisyllabic Suwawa words whose stress falls on the last syllable (ultima), the second from the end (penult), and the third from the end (antepenult). [moho'ha] 'astonished' ... [bu'lawa] 'gold' ... ['watopo] 'roof'
new_statements.citation: Rangubang, J., N. Panrelli-Adrah, N. Pesik, R. Paath & W. Palar. 2001. Fonologi Bahasa Suwawa. Jakarta: Pusat Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan Nasional.
new_statements.locator: Bab III, section 3.4 'Unsur Suprasegmental', printed pp. 55-56 (pp. 66-67); examples continue to p. 57; restated in Bab V Simpulan item 11, pp. 87-88
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Copies checked (121 pp., complete, scanned text; extracted text dump) and 152 pp., complete). QUOTE: I rendered pp. 66-67 (printed pp. 55-56) of Rangubang et al. 2001 as images and read them directly. Section 3.4 'Unsur Suprasegmental' reads exactly: 'Berdasarkan data yang dikumpulkan, tidak dijumpai adanya tekanan, nada, dan panjang pendeknya bunyi yang dapat mengubah arti suatu kata. Walaupun demikian, tidak dapat dikatakan bahwa tekanan dalam bahasa Suwawa tidak fonemis. Dengan demikian, tekanan pada bahasa Suwawa tidak tetap atau tidak dapat diprakirakan. Artinya, tekanan dalam bahasa Suwawa tidak seperti dalam bahasa Indonesia yang pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku kedua dari belaka…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Per the 2001 phonology: word-stress position is not fixed and not predictable from the word shape; in trisyllabic words it may fall on the final ([moho'ha], [ogi'na], [togu'bi]), the penult ([ti'gogo], [to'mita], [bu'lawa], [mo'puha], [ti'ama] etc., the largest group) or the antepenult (['watopo], ['dapugo], ['putodo], ['wandogo], ['alipo], ['bibigo] etc.); no minimal pairs distinguished by stress were found, yet the authors 'consider stress phonemic' because its place is unpredictable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said about secondary stress in either source.
new_statements.exceptions: The older grammar sketch Kasim et al. 1981 (Struktur Bahasa Suwawa, sec. 3.5, pp. 22-23, same folder) gives a different, predictable account in terms of syllable pitch: 'Nada itu ditentukan oleh jumlah suku kata. (1) Bila terdiri dari dua suku kata maka nada tinggi terdapat pada suku kedua dari belakang [wúlu 'kepala', wígu 'mandi']. (2) Bila terdiri dari tiga suku kata maka nada tinggi pada suku ketiga dari belakang [dútuna 'sungai', wáteya 'saya']. (3) Bila terdiri dari empat suku kata maka nada tinggi tetap pada suku ketiga dari belakang [peyábuqo 'debu', tobúnggala 'kebun']' = high pitch on the antepenult (penult/initial in disyllables). Rangubang 2001's trisyllabic penult and ultima examples ([bu'lawa], [ti'gogo], [moho'ha]) directly contradict rule (2), though both agree on ['watopo] (1981 writes /wa:topo/ with a long antepenult vowel). Many 2001 antepenult items end in what looks like a paragogic -o after a historical final consonant (watopo 'atap', alipo 'kulit', bibigo 'bibir'), and several penult items carry prefixes (mo-puha, ti-ama), so a morphology/history-conditioned regularity may underlie the 'unpredictable' surface pattern; neither source analyses this.
new_statements.domain_note: Both sources describe isolated citation forms elicited from a wordlist (2001: 651-item list, six speakers from Bube, Duano, Tingkohubu villages, Kec. Suwawa; transcribed by ear, recordings made). 2001 speaks of 'tekanan' (stress); 1981 frames the same prominence as syllable pitch level ('titi nada', levels 1-4) and says Suwawa speech sounds 'tersentak-sentak' (jerky) because one syllable per word carries high pitch. Word domain; nothing on phrase-level prosody beyond 1981's remark on interrogative intonation.
new_statements.identity_note: Both sources describe Suwawa proper as spoken in Kecamatan Suwawa (Bube, Duano/Bunedaa, Tingkohubu etc.), Gorontalo = Glottolog suwa1241 / ISO swu; Kasim 1981 also sampled two villages in Kec. Bonepantai (Bilungala), i.e. the Bune Bonda/Bonda variety, which Glottolog files under the same languoid. Rangubang 2001 states the population is dialectally homogeneous.

new_statements.quote: Berbeda dengan bahasa Inggris, misalnya, tekanan dalam bahasa Bonda tidak membedakan makna. Namun, kalau diamat-amati, tekanan dalam bahasa Bonda jatuh pada suku kedua dari belakang (penultima). Contoh: anáma 'kemenyan', dutúna 'sungai', wadála 'kuda', kuukúdo 'kudis', maanúqo 'ayam', putóngi 'pipi'. [p. 20:] Baik nada maupun lagu, tidak membedakan makna dalam bahasa Bonda. [p. 20, d. Panjang:] Unsur suprasegmental berupa panjang (length) banyak kami temui dalam bahasa Bonda. Unsur suprasegmental berupa panjang tersebut terdapat pada suku pertama atau kedua bentuk dasar.
new_statements.translation: Unlike English, for example, stress in Bonda does not distinguish meaning. However, on close observation, stress in Bonda falls on the second syllable from the end (the penult). Examples: anáma 'incense', dutúna 'river', wadála 'horse', kuukúdo 'scabies', maanúqo 'chicken', putóngi 'cheek'. [p. 20:] Neither pitch nor intonation distinguishes meaning in Bonda. [p. 20:] The suprasegmental element of length is frequently found in Bonda; it occurs on the first or second syllable of the base.

Namun, kalau diamat-amati, tekanan dalam bahasa Bonda jatuh pada suku kedua dari belakang (penultima).' -- the text garbles the example words, so I rendered p. 3…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Suwawa is a 'conflict' built from Rangubang et al. 2001 (stress 'tidak tetap atau tidak dapat diprakirakan.. tidak seperti dalam bahasa Indonesia yang pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku kedua dari belakang' = not fixed/predictable, explicitly not penultimate) and Kasim et al. 1981 (sec. 3.5: high pitch on the penult in disyllables but on the antepenult in words of three or more syllables, e.g. dútuna 'sungai'). Tome et al. 1988 states a third position: non-contrastive stress fixed on the penult, and marks the same word as dutúna 'sungai' with penultimate stress, directly against Kasim et al.'s antepenultimate marking and against Rangubang et al.'s 'not penultimate,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable (all six illustrative words, of two to four syllables, are marked with penultimate stress); pitch and intonation are likewise non-contrastive; vowel length occurs on the first or second syllable of a base and is retained (shifting one syllable rightward in linear count) under prefixation.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the statement is hedged only by 'kalau diamat-amati' (on close observation). The book states (p. 6) that it does not treat Bonda phonology in full, only phonemicisation and spelling, so the stress remark is a brief observation inside a morphology.
new_statements.identity_note: Tome et al. 1988 describe 'bahasa Bonda' = the language now known as Suwawa, spoken in Kecamatan Suwawa and Kecamatan Bonepantai (Gorontalo), data from villages Bube, Duano, Dumbayabulan, Bilungala, Taludaa, fieldwork 1982/1983 (sec. 1.5, p. 2; p. 20 'ciri orang Suwawa'); 'Bune Bonda'/'Bonda' is the indigenous name (Sneddon & Usup 1986: 409). Same language as the catalog entry suwa1241.

readall_conflicts: Among the sources already held by the project for this item there is a standing tension the catalog should keep in view: Rangubang et al. 2001 (sec. 3.4, pp. 55-57) say stress is not fixed and not predictable and treat it as phonemic, with three-syllable examples stressed on the ultima, penult and antepenult, whereas Kasim et al. 1981 (sec. 3.5, pp. 22-23) describe a fixed pattern of high pitch ('titi nada') on the penult in two-syllable words and on the antepenult in three- and four-syllable words. Sneddon & Usup 1986 do not settle this for Suwawa; their Buol/Kaidipang pattern (penult, antepenult before a paragogic vowel) resembles the Kasim 1981 description, and their footnote's 'unpredictable' label resembles Rangubang 2001, but they say nothing about Suwawa itself. Three Pusat Bahasa descriptions of Suwawa/Bonda prosody disagree on placement while agreeing that stress/pitch is not meaning-distinguishing: Kasim et al. 1981 (Struktur Bahasa Suwawa, sec. 3.5) puts the high pitch on the penult in disyllables and on the antepenult in longer words (dútuna 'sungai'); Tome et al. 1988 (Morfologi Dialek Bune Bonda, sec. 2.4.3, p. 19, newly obtained and read here) says stress falls on the penult and marks dutúna, kuukúdo, maanúqo, putóngi with penultimate stress; Rangubang et al. 2001 (Fonologi Bahasa Suwawa, sec. 3.4) says stress is not fixed or predictable and explicitly unlike Indonesian penultimate stress. The new source therefore contradicts both legs of the catalog's existin…

sources.note: Sec. 3.5 'Suprasegmental', pp. 22-23: treats word prominence as syllabic pitch ('titi nada'); high pitch position 'ditentukan oleh jumlah suku kata': disyllables -> penult (wúlu 'kepala', wígu 'mandi'); trisyllables -> third from end (dútuna 'sungai', wáteya 'saya'); four-syllable words -> still third from end (peyábuqo 'debu', tobúnggala 'kebun'). I.e. a syllable-count rule (antepenult, penult=initial in disyllables). Morphology chapter writes long vowels on that syllable (/wa:topo/ 'atap', /moga:topo/). CONTRADICTS Rangubang 2001's 'unpredictable' statement and its penult/ultima trisyllabic…
